o: Inheritance of both chromosomes of a pair from one parent
Having three copies of a chromosome
qs.e: Uniparental disomy is the inheritance of both chromosomes of a pair from one parent. In Prader-Willi syndrome, this can occur when both copies of chromosome 15 are from the mother.
qs.s: SINGLE-GENE DISORDERS WITH ATYPICAL INHERITANCE MCQs

qs.q: Why can Prader-Willi syndrome result from maternal uniparental disomy of chromosome 15?
o: Patient lacks functional genes from nonimprinted paternal chromosome
qs.e: Maternal uniparental disomy means the patient has both copies from the mother and lacks functional genes from the nonimprinted paternal chromosome 15, resulting in the same effect as paternal deletion.
qs.s: SINGLE-GENE DISORDERS WITH ATYPICAL INHERITANCE MCQs

qs.q: In Prader-Willi syndrome caused by maternal uniparental disomy of chromosome 15, why are paternally expressed genes absent?
o: Both chromosome 15 copies are maternal and the relevant maternal alleles are normally imprinted
Both chromosome 15 copies are paternal and therefore silenced
Chromosome 15 is absent from all cells
All genes on chromosome 15 are normally inactive
qs.e: In the relevant imprinted region, paternally expressed genes are normally active only from the paternal chromosome. Maternal uniparental disomy leaves two maternal copies, so those paternal-expression genes are functionally absent.
qs.s: SINGLE-GENE DISORDERS WITH ATYPICAL INHERITANCE MCQs
